# naming.numeric.units-wide-frontier

Kind: `native-observation`

## Problem statement

An original String and a ByteArray containing the same bytes can materialize different native strings before a failing getter. Primitive error formatting and outer script error publication also have different byte frontiers.

## Question

For seven malformed/astral/long native inputs as original String versus ByteArray, what wide getter cache, primitive/result message and errorCode are observed?

## Conclusion

Every reached wide control fails. Original String bytes and ByteArray native-string materialization are separately retained, including C9 invalid-byte mapping and release-specific long diagnostic excerpts. Primitive/message/errorCode fields record the exact stage; the observation does not grant a compiler source or Unicode display producer.

## Scope

C public original-object wide getter is reached by one native callback from ASCII Tcl_Eval. Exact source bytes and selected storage/priming axes are retained; primitive result is duplicated before the callback returns, and final result/cache/errorCode/original input bytes are then sampled. Seven cases×String/ByteArray, fourteen rows per selected getter. Capture source/library/executable/row count/run0 are recorded; original C output checksums, headers/compiler status/configure/runtime patch query were not recorded by these receipts. Retained streams have current permanent evidence hashes. BIG-IP is not tested; Jim is only measured for seeded fresh Strings.
